correctness.rationale: The intensity coefficient of order k is 2 Re(a_k exp(ikφ)) plus a real quadratic term using indices 1 through k−1 only. Back substitution in (Re a_k, Im a_k) therefore gives a real polynomial inverse for every real data vector exactly when the diagonal blocks of determinant −4 sin(kθ) are invertible. The converse addresses genuine injectivity, not just derivative degeneracy: at a resonance the two polynomials 1±iz^k have identical full intensities. Removing any one of the reported data coordinates from a bijection onto all of R^(2N) loses injectivity. The block lower triangular determinant holds for every input, and at p=1 all off-diagonal blocks vanish. The two squared singular values per order are 4(1±|cos(kθ)|). Letting α=θ/π reduces the smallest singular value optimization to maximizing the closest circular distance to zero among kα, 1≤k≤N. A collision gives distance zero. Otherwise the minimum pair distance among the N+1 points equals the smallest circular gap, since all positive arc sums are at least that gap; differences exhaust the kα distances. The gaps sum to one, with equality in the bound only for a uniform grid. With 0 included, α must be a primitive generator of that grid, and every such generator works. The sine product follows from differentiating z^(N+1)−1 at z=1 and taking absolute values of the factors, giving |det|=2^N(N+1). For N=1 the same argument gives the single right-angle optimum. Read the stated sum of squared moduli as the squared Euclidean input norm, as fixed by the real-coordinate Jacobian and Euclidean singular-value calculation.
residual_risks: The verification note overstates primitive-grid sampling: checker.py line 32 chooses the first coprime numerator, always 1, for each tested N. It uses floating-point comparisons, not exact symbolic reconstruction; its resonance test compares jets only. The general arithmetic, exact inverse and full intensity ambiguity are proved analytically, not inferred from those checks.
The optimum pertains to the specified unweighted Euclidean differential at p=1 only, not global noise stability.

value.rationale: The exact jet map is a natural finite-dimensional measurement model motivated by phase retrieval, and the design target is the worst-direction differential of that specific model. Rational lines, usually discussed as ambiguous in the unrestricted setting, can be not only valid but exactly optimal for any given degree. Identifying all primitive designs and the sharp singular value gives a usable benchmark for local noise amplification at the constant polynomial rather than a qualitative uniqueness restatement.
residual_risks: Exact Taylor data and this Euclidean normalization are essential; no claim is made about noisy point sampling, other metrics or other coefficient-space locations.
